original.target_description: Study 4: stainless steel mug advertisement oriented to match versus mismatch dominant hand; online-panel participants; one-factor ANOVA of amount of embodied mental simulation (three-item scale).

n.sample_role: Online-panel participants completing Study 4; analytic sample for the one-factor ANOVA, corroborated by F(1, 76).
n.exclusions: No exclusions or missing-data losses reported for Study 4; 78 completers and error df 76 support all completers in this test.
n.location: Published article p. 998 (PDF page 11), Study 4, Design and Procedure; Results.
n.quote: Seventy-eight partici- ... pants from an online panel completed the study in exchange ... for monetary compensation.

es.location: Published article p. 998 (PDF page 11), Study 4, Results; orientation match versus mismatch ANOVA.

p.location: Published article p. 998 (PDF page 11), Study 4, Results; orientation match versus mismatch ANOVA.

replication.target_description: Relationship between visual product depictions in advertisements, including orientation toward the participant’s dominant hand, and mental simulation, in the context of purchase intention. Japanese online adult sample; full-sample ANOVA.

n.sample_role: Japanese online participants included in final analysis
n.exclusions: 247 excluded for failing instructional manipulation check and attention check question; paper recruitment statement says 1000, inconsistent with 823 + 247.
n.quote: Finally, the data of 823 participants (mean age = 40.77, SD of age = 10.48, 428 males, 391 females, 4 did not prefer to say) were analyzed.

reported_success.quote: No studies involving visual factors, between-participant manipulation of senses, or interactions between factors could be replicated.

notes:
Reported success is the authors’ study-level verdict. 
Source follow-up: Fresh original-only extraction from supplied published JCR article, 38(6), 988–1003 (2012 issue; 2011 copyright/online publication retained). Title and authors match supplied reference. Rendered PDF page 11 inspected: canonical text uses p for printed equals signs and ! for printed less-than signs; quotations retain these exact text-layer glyphs. Explicit ellipses omit interleaved text from the other column while retaining line-end hyphenation. No metric conversion. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. Target is amount of mental simulation, not the separately reported ease-of-simulation test (F = 3.20, p = .08), nor the mediator-to-purchase-intentions regression. The rendered article says mismatch led to greater ease although its printed means run the other way; this wording discrepancy does not affect the amount-of-simulation target.
